note: Each claim is one rendered observation on the canonical page. A null or absent figure mints no claim — absence is never zero. Scheme: https://terralore.co/integrity

claims.title: Shang dynasty rules the Yellow River valley
claims.summary: The Shang, the first Chinese dynasty with historical records, governs from cities such as Anyang and produces ritual bronzes and the oracle-bone script, the earliest known Chinese writing.

sources.label: Zhou dynasty (ca. 1050-221 BCE), Teaching China with the Smithsonian
sources.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-1600bce-shang-dynasty-rules-the-yellow-river-valley, claim TL:CHN:event:1600bce:shang-dynasty-rules-the-yellow-river-valley, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Oracle-bone divination records
claims.summary: Shang diviners inscribe questions to ancestors and deities on ox bones and turtle shells; these inscriptions are the oldest unambiguous Chinese writing and a primary source for early history.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-1200bce-oracle-bone-divination-records, claim TL:CHN:event:1200bce:oracle-bone-divination-records, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Zhou conquest and the Mandate of Heaven
claims.summary: King Wu of Zhou defeats the Shang at the Battle of Muye and founds the Zhou dynasty, justifying the overthrow with the Mandate of Heaven, a doctrine of morally conditional rule that endures for millennia.

sources.label: Zhou dynasty (ca. 1050-221 BCE), Teaching China with the Smithsonian
sources.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-1046bce-zhou-conquest-and-the-mandate-of-heaven, claim TL:CHN:event:1046bce:zhou-conquest-and-the-mandate-of-heaven, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Western Zhou collapses; Eastern Zhou begins
claims.summary: Nomadic invasions force the Zhou court to flee east to Luoyang in 771 BCE, beginning the Eastern Zhou and a long decline of royal authority into the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods.

sources.label: Zhou dynasty (ca. 1050-221 BCE), Teaching China with the Smithsonian
sources.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-771bce-western-zhou-collapses-eastern-zhou-begins, claim TL:CHN:event:771bce:western-zhou-collapses-eastern-zhou-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Lifetime of Confucius
claims.summary: Confucius (551-479 BCE) teaches that social order rests on moral cultivation, ritual, and proper human relationships; his thought becomes the dominant ethical tradition of imperial China.

sources.label: Zhou dynasty (ca. 1050-221 BCE), Teaching China with the Smithsonian
sources.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-551bce-lifetime-of-confucius, claim TL:CHN:event:551bce:lifetime-of-confucius, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Qin unifies China; the First Emperor is proclaimed
claims.summary: Qin completes its conquest of the Warring States and its king takes the title Shi Huangdi, founding the first unified Chinese empire and the centralized bureaucratic system that defines imperial China.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-221bce-qin-unifies-china-the-first-emperor-is, claim TL:CHN:event:221bce:qin-unifies-china-the-first-emperor-is, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Frontier walls joined into the Great Wall
claims.summary: Under the First Emperor, earlier northern fortifications are connected into a unified defense against steppe invasions, the origin of the Great Wall that later dynasties would expand.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-214bce-frontier-walls-joined-into-the-great-wall, claim TL:CHN:event:214bce:frontier-walls-joined-into-the-great-wall, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of the First Emperor and the terracotta army
claims.summary: Qin Shi Huang dies and is entombed near Xi'an in a colossal mausoleum guarded by roughly 8,000 terracotta warriors, rediscovered in 1974 and now a UNESCO World Heritage site.

sources.label: Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor (World Heritage List)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-210bce-death-of-the-first-emperor-and-the-terracotta, claim TL:CHN:event:210bce:death-of-the-first-emperor-and-the-terracotta, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Han dynasty consolidates the empire
claims.summary: After the Qin collapse, the Han dynasty (206 BCE-220 CE) institutionalizes Confucian-trained bureaucracy and the civil service, giving China its enduring model of imperial government and the name of its majority people.

sources.label: Han dynasty (206 BCE-220 CE), Teaching China with the Smithsonian
sources.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-206bce-han-dynasty-consolidates-the-empire, claim TL:CHN:event:206bce:han-dynasty-consolidates-the-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Silk Road trade routes open under Emperor Wu
claims.summary: Emperor Wu's campaigns against the Xiongnu and missions into Central Asia open the overland Silk Road, linking China to India, Persia, and the Mediterranean in exchange of goods and ideas.

sources.label: Han dynasty (206 BCE-220 CE), Teaching China with the Smithsonian
sources.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-138bce-silk-road-trade-routes-open-under-emperor-wu, claim TL:CHN:event:138bce:silk-road-trade-routes-open-under-emperor-wu, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Collapse of the Han and centuries of division
claims.summary: The Han empire fragments into the Three Kingdoms and successive Northern and Southern Dynasties, a long era of disunion during which Buddhism takes deep root in China.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-220-collapse-of-the-han-and-centuries-of-division, claim TL:CHN:event:220:collapse-of-the-han-and-centuries-of-division, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sui dynasty reunifies China
claims.summary: The Sui (581-618) reunite north and south and build the Grand Canal, restoring a centralized empire after centuries of division and setting the stage for the Tang golden age.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-589-sui-dynasty-reunifies-china, claim TL:CHN:event:589:sui-dynasty-reunifies-china, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Tang dynasty and a cosmopolitan golden age
claims.summary: The Tang dynasty (618-907) builds a vast, outward-looking empire centered on Chang'an, refining the examination system and producing a flowering of poetry; woodblock printing and gunpowder first appear.

sources.label: Tang dynasty, Teaching China with the Smithsonian
sources.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art

sources.label: Song Dynasty and the golden age (Asia for Educators)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-618-tang-dynasty-and-a-cosmopolitan-golden-age, claim TL:CHN:event:618:tang-dynasty-and-a-cosmopolitan-golden-age, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Song dynasty and a commercial revolution
claims.summary: The Song dynasty (960-1279) presides over an economic and technological boom, introducing movable-type printing, government paper money, the navigational compass, and gunpowder weapons.

sources.label: Song Dynasty and the golden age (Asia for Educators)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-960-song-dynasty-and-a-commercial-revolution, claim TL:CHN:event:960:song-dynasty-and-a-commercial-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kublai Khan founds the Mongol Yuan dynasty
claims.summary: Kublai Khan declares the Yuan dynasty in 1271 and completes the conquest of the Song by 1279, ruling China from Dadu (Beijing) as the first foreign-led dynasty to govern all of China.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-1271-kublai-khan-founds-the-mongol-yuan-dynasty, claim TL:CHN:event:1271:kublai-khan-founds-the-mongol-yuan-dynasty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ming dynasty restores Han rule
claims.summary: Zhu Yuanzhang overthrows the Yuan and founds the Ming dynasty (1368-1644), which rebuilds the Great Wall in stone, constructs the Forbidden City, and revives Han Chinese imperial governance.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-1368-ming-dynasty-restores-han-rule, claim TL:CHN:event:1368:ming-dynasty-restores-han-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Zheng He's maritime voyages
claims.summary: The Ming admiral Zheng He leads seven vast treasure-fleet expeditions across Southeast Asia, the Indian Ocean, and the coast of Africa, projecting Chinese power before the dynasty turns inward.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-1405-zheng-he-s-maritime-voyages, claim TL:CHN:event:1405:zheng-he-s-maritime-voyages, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Manchus establish the Qing dynasty
claims.summary: The Manchus capture Beijing and found the Qing dynasty (1644-1912), China's last imperial dynasty, which expands the empire to its greatest extent under the Kangxi and Qianlong emperors.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-1644-manchus-establish-the-qing-dynasty, claim TL:CHN:event:1644:manchus-establish-the-qing-dynasty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First Opium War and the 'unequal treaties'
claims.summary: War with Britain over the opium trade ends in Qing defeat and the Treaty of Nanjing (1842), ceding Hong Kong and opening treaty ports, the start of a century of foreign encroachment China calls its century of humiliation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-1839-first-opium-war-and-the-unequal-treaties, claim TL:CHN:event:1839:first-opium-war-and-the-unequal-treaties, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Xinhai Revolution erupts
claims.summary: The Wuchang Uprising of 10 October 1911 sparks the Xinhai Revolution against the Qing, rapidly spreading across the provinces and bringing down China's last imperial dynasty.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-1911-xinhai-revolution-erupts, claim TL:CHN:event:1911:xinhai-revolution-erupts, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Republic of China founded; last emperor abdicates
claims.summary: Sun Yat-sen becomes provisional president of the Republic of China on 1 January 1912, and on 12 February the child emperor Puyi abdicates, ending more than two millennia of imperial rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-1912-republic-of-china-founded-last-emperor-abdicates, claim TL:CHN:event:1912:republic-of-china-founded-last-emperor-abdicates, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Warlord Era of political fragmentation
claims.summary: The death of Yuan Shikai in 1916 plunges China into the Warlord Era, with regional militarists ruling much of the country until the Nationalists reassert partial unity by 1928.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-1916-warlord-era-of-political-fragmentation, claim TL:CHN:event:1916:warlord-era-of-political-fragmentation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Second Sino-Japanese War and the Nanjing Massacre
claims.summary: Japan's full-scale invasion from July 1937 brings catastrophic violence, including the December 1937 Nanjing Massacre, in which Japanese forces murdered many tens of thousands of civilians and prisoners and committed mass rape.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-1937-second-sino-japanese-war-and-the-nanjing, claim TL:CHN:event:1937:second-sino-japanese-war-and-the-nanjing, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Chinese Civil War resumes; Communist victory
claims.summary: After Japan's surrender, full-scale civil war between Nationalists and Communists resumes, ending in 1949 with Communist victory and the retreat of Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalist government to Taiwan.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-1946-chinese-civil-war-resumes-communist-victory, claim TL:CHN:event:1946:chinese-civil-war-resumes-communist-victory, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: People's Republic of China proclaimed
claims.summary: Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic of China from the Tiananmen gate in Beijing on 1 October 1949, with Zhou Enlai as premier, after Communist victory in the civil war.

sources.label: Mao Zedong Proclaims a Communist People's Republic in China

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-1949-people-s-republic-of-china-proclaimed, claim TL:CHN:event:1949:people-s-republic-of-china-proclaimed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Great Leap Forward and the great famine
claims.summary: Mao's Great Leap Forward forces rapid collectivization and crude industrialization, causing a famine from 1959 to 1961 that killed an estimated 15 million to tens of millions of people.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-1958-great-leap-forward-and-the-great-famine, claim TL:CHN:event:1958:great-leap-forward-and-the-great-famine, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cultural Revolution
claims.summary: Mao launches the Cultural Revolution, a decade of political persecution, purges, and social upheaval that convulses Chinese society until his death in 1976.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-1966-cultural-revolution, claim TL:CHN:event:1966:cultural-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Deng Xiaoping launches reform and opening
claims.summary: Under Deng Xiaoping, China begins 'reform and opening' in 1978, decollectivizing agriculture and embracing markets and foreign investment, igniting decades of rapid economic growth.

sources.label: How China Transformed Under Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-1978-deng-xiaoping-launches-reform-and-opening, claim TL:CHN:event:1978:deng-xiaoping-launches-reform-and-opening, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Tiananmen Square crackdown
claims.summary: The army violently suppresses pro-democracy demonstrations centered on Beijing's Tiananmen Square in June 1989, killing many protesters and reasserting tight Communist Party political control.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of China: Four thousand years of civilization, from oracle-bone kings to the world's second-largest economy.", terralore.co/country/CHN/chronicle#ev-1989-tiananmen-square-crackdown, claim TL:CHN:event:1989:tiananmen-square-crackdown, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
